Article Title: 23 Himveers battle weeks of gruelling Himalayan climbing to reach 24,131-ft Mt Abi Gamin & unfurl Tricolour
Article Text:
23 ITBP Himveers have scaled Uttarakhand’s 7,355 metre Mt Abi Gamin.

A mountain near the frontier

NEW DELHI: 23 ITBP personnel conquered the 7,355-metre Mt Abi Gamin on the Indo-Tibet frontier in Uttarakhand, reaching its summit on September 16 and unfurling the Tricolour at an altitude of about 24,131 feet.Led by deputy commandant Parikshit Shah, the team began its expedition from ITBP headquarters in New Delhi on August 7. The climb took weeks of preparation, acclimatisation and movement through the difficult terrain of the Garhwal Himalayas.The expedition was part of the Force Level Mountaineering Expedition 2026 and was flagged off by ITBP director general Shatrujeet Kapur.At more than 7,000 metres, Abi Gamin presents a combination of thin air, freezing temperatures, snow and glacier terrain. Weather conditions can also change rapidly at such heights.The ITBP said the expedition demonstrated the force's mountaineering skills, determination and team spirit. After weeks on the mountain, the team finally reached the summit on September 16.The official ITBP account marked the achievement with the words, “Himveers summit Mt Abi Gamin!”, while highlighting the 23-member team's mountaineering skills, determination and team spirit.DG Shatrujeet Kapur also congratulated the expedition members.Mt Abi Gamin, also known as Ibi Gamin, is located in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district in the Garhwal Himalayas. It is close to Mt Kamet, with its summit located on the India-Tibet frontier and its northern slopes extending towards Tibet.The mountain is roughly 2 km northeast of Kamet and forms part of the wider Kamet massif.Abi Gamin has a long history of mountaineering. An Anglo-Swiss expedition made the first successful ascent in 1950 after approaching the mountain from the Tibetan side through Mana Pass. Indian mountaineers also successfully climbed it in the 1950s, including an expedition led by Nandu Jayal in 1953.Its location adds significance to the ITBP expedition, as the force has personnel operating regularly in high-altitude Himalayan areas.The challenge at more than 24,000 feet goes beyond the steepness of the mountain. Oxygen levels are much lower than at sea level, while extreme cold, snow, glaciers and sudden weather changes can make movement dangerous.The route around Abi Gamin has historically involved snow and glacier sections, with the mountain linked to nearby Kamet through Meade's Col. Earlier expeditions have reported difficult ice sections and extremely cold conditions at high camps.Such conditions make acclimatisation, careful planning and experience essential for any expedition to the summit.
Article Summary: 23 ITBP Himveers have scaled Uttarakhand’s 7,355 metre Mt Abi Gamin. The climb took weeks of preparation, acclimatisation and movement through the difficult terrain of the Garhwal Himalayas. The ITBP said the expedition demonstrated the force's mountaineering skills, determination and team spirit.

Article Title: Vote chori protest: Gaurav Gogoi, other Congress leaders detained; cops use water cannons in Patna, Chandigarh

NEW DELHI: Assam Congress chief Gaurav Gogoi and several party leaders were detained during a protest in Guwahati on Friday demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The detentions came as Congress workers staged demonstrations in several states over the functioning of the Election Commission.The Jantar mantar protest site has been closed for protestors whereas police used water cannons to disperse protesters in Chandigarh and Patna during the demonstrations.Security personnel were also deployed outside the Election Commission office in New Delhi ahead of a Delhi Congress demonstration over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The Indian Youth Congress was also scheduled to march from Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar.The protests follow an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR process. The report said their concerns included voter registration, deletion and restoration of names and access to electoral-roll databases.The Madhya Pradesh Youth Congress held a protest outside the Chief Electoral Officer’s office in Bhopal on Thursday, demanding Kumar’s resignation. Protesters raised slogans against the CEC and carried posters reading “arrest Gyanesh Kumar for treason” and “Vote-Chori magic trick exposed”.In Dehradun, Congress workers also staged a protest demanding Kumar’s resignation, with Congress MP Kumari Selja leading the demonstration.In Punjab, Pradesh Congress Committee president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring demanded Kumar’s dismissal, an FIR against him and his alleged collaborators, and their arrest. He also announced a march to the ECI office in Chandigarh under the leadership of Sachin Pilot.In Karnataka, the Pradesh Congress Committee filed a police complaint seeking action against Kumar and BJP MLA Abhay Patil over alleged violations of voting rights and alleged attempts to manipulate electoral rolls. Congress alleged that Patil had sought deletion of eligible voters’ names and sought penal action against Kumar over alleged arbitrary deletions.Congress workers in Kolkata, West Bengal also staged a protest demanding the resignation of Kumar.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Friday said his organisation would launch nationwide protests from October 2 if Kumar did not resign by Saturday.In a post on X, Dipke said CJP would begin its protest from Mumbai on Gandhi Jayanti and subsequently take the agitation to cities across India.“If Gyanesh Kumar does not resign by tomorrow, CJP will begin its nationwide protest from Mumbai on 2 October, and take it to cities across India. This Gandhi Jayanti let’s pledge to save democracy,” Dipke wrote.The announcement came a day after Dipke demanded Kumar’s resignation and threatened a “Jantar Mantar 2.0” agitation if his demand was not met.The Indian Youth Congress on Thursday launched a nationwide online citizens’ petition titled “Gyanesh, It’s Done Bro”, seeking action against Kumar and urging citizens, particularly young people, to participate in a campaign for electoral transparency and accountability.The IYC has demanded Kumar’s removal as CEC, along with his arrest and prosecution. It has also sought a comprehensive investigation into electoral-roll processes, the alleged BJP connection raised by the campaign, and the release of electoral records and internal objections.Opposition plans removal motionOpposition parties are also preparing to move a motion seeking Kumar’s removal in both Houses of Parliament, with Congress reaching out to other opposition parties, party sources said. The notice is expected to be submitted in the coming days. A similar move is being prepared as the political dispute over the ECI and SIR continues.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday alleged with “100 per cent certainty” that elections in India, including the 2024 Lok Sabha polls and several Assembly contests, had been “rigged”. He demanded Kumar’s resignation and alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah were at the top of a conspiracy and would face investigation.“The first thing we are saying is Mr. Gyanesh Kumar must resign immediately... This thing that you have done is an act against the Indian nation... A person who attacks the vote, who fundamentally destroys India's democratic institution, is nothing other than a 'Desh Drohi',” Gandhi said.He also said the CEC should “turn Approver”.In Raipur, All India Adivasi Congress president Vikrant Bhuria defended Gandhi’s allegations of “vote theft”, saying they were based on facts.“Whatever Rahul Gandhi says is based on facts, and history bears witness that every claim he has made has eventually been proven true. We had been campaigning for quite some time, under his leadership, against vote theft, highlighting that votes were being stolen, elections were being rigged, names were being deleted from voter lists, and the names of ineligible people were being added,” Bhuria told ANI.“Instances were found where thousands of voters were registered at a single address. He substantiated these claims with facts, yet the Election Commission failed to take cognizance of them,” he added.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra defended Rahul Gandhi’s allegations and rejected the BJP’s response to the controversy.“I'm sorry, that's a very stale and weak story. There are facts, there is evidence. It is there for the whole country to see. My brother (Rahul Gandhi) has shown it in many different press conferences. He has put the evidence forward. Now it is very clear. 13 crore voters have been deleted. This is a lame excuse, and the BJP should stop making lame excuses. If they are meddling with our elections and if their leadership is making the Election Commission do this, then it is an act of treason and they should be aware of it. ..They are doing an illegal act. How many years has it been that they have been rigging elections? Naturally, they are so overconfident all the time...”Asked whether Congress was planning a protest, she said, “There is a CWC meeting, I think, for which I am having to go back. So they will decide on that meeting and suppose what the course of action will be.”The Election Commission has rejected the assertion that objections raised by Sandhu and Joshi represented structural or institutional dissent over final decisions. The poll panel has said operational queries, internal feedback and administrative suggestions raised during the drafting process are part of the normal functioning of a multi-member constitutional body. It has maintained that all final decisions, including those related to SIR, were unanimous.The ECI has also said ECINet is a secure, decentralised digital platform operated under the Representation of the People Acts, 1950 and 1951. According to the poll panel, statutory duties on the platform are carried out by designated field officers, including BLOs, AEROs, EROs, DEOs and CEOs, using unique IDs and secure credentials.Union minister Chirag Paswan said that if questions are being raised about the Election Commission, an independent constitutional body, the responsibility lies with the CEC to present his position clearly.“If questions are being raised on Election Commission, which is an independent constitutional body, responsibility lies with CEC to present his stance clearly. It is problematic if people begin to doubt electoral process itself. EC needs to present its stance, not to Rahul Gandhi, but to public,” Paswan said.The controversy over the SIR exercise and the ECI’s internal functioning is expected to be taken up at the Congress Working Committee meeting scheduled for September 29 in New Delhi.A plea filed in the Supreme Court has challenged alleged unilateral decisions taken by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in connection with the Election Commission’s electoral-roll revision exercise, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).The petitioner has sought an SIT investigation into the alleged deletion of around 13 crore voters from electoral rolls. The plea also seeks a declaration that decisions allegedly taken without the concurrence of the other two Election Commissioners were illegal.It has further sought restoration of the original Form 6 used for voter registration and prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar, Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg and ECI IT head Seema Khanna for alleged violations of their duties under the Representation of the People Act.
Article Summary: Water cannons used on Congress protesters in Chandigarh, Patna. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke threatens nationwide protests if Gyanesh Kumar does not resign by Saturday. Opposition parties preparing to move motion seeking Kumar’s removal in both Houses of Parliament.

NEW DELHI: A plea has been filed in the Supreme Court against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged unilateral decisions taken in connection with the Election Commission (ECI) electoral roll revision exercise, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll. The petitioner has also sought a Special Investigation Team (SIT) inquiry into the alleged deletion of around 13 crore voters from electoral rolls.The plea seeks a declaration that decisions allegedly taken without the concurrence of the other two election commissioners are illegal and calls for restoration of the original Form 6 used for voter registration. It also seeks prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar, deputy election commissioner Maneesh Garg and ECI IT head Seema Khanna for alleged violations of duties under the Representation of the People Act.The petition follows a report by The Indian Express stating that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions concerning the addition, deletion and restoration of voters and changes to the voter registration process.The petitioner has sought prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act.EC has maintained that all decisions, including those relating to SIR, were unanimous and taken with the approval of both Election Commissioners and the CEC.
Article Summary: A plea has been filed in the Supreme Court against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. NEW DELHI: US mercenary Aaron VanDyke, who was arrested by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) earlier this year in the Myanmar terror training case, was released from the Tihar jail after after a special NIA court granted permission to travel to the USA to meet their families for one month.The NIA court, along with Matthew Aaron Vandyke, gave permission to 6 Ukrainian nationals to travel to Ukraine subject to certain conditions and formalities.The court directed the release of their passports to them. NEW DELHI: A fresh landslide in Rimbi village under the Yuksom-Tashiding constituency of West Sikkim triggered a mudslide on Friday, sending large amounts of mud, rocks and debris downhill amid continued rainfall.The landslide has raised concerns among residents as nearby houses, properties and road connectivity remain at risk. Article Title: 'Dubai-based scammers looted Rs 94,000 crore': CBI arrests Mahadev app key accused deported from UAE

CBI on Thursday arrested Abhishek Kumar, a key accused in the Mahadev online betting and gambling case in which Enforcement Directorate (ED) has claimed that the perpetrators of the illegal activities have so far generated and laundered proceeds of crime of more than Rs 94,000 crore.Kumar was deported from the UAE and taken into custody by CBI immediately after he arrived at Hyderabad airport from Dubai. He was close to main accused Saurabh Chandrakar and Shubham Soni - both continue to operate the gambling network from the UAE and other jurisdictions.Kumar coordinated various panels in the Mahadev network and was responsible for collecting funds and acquiring immovable assets in Dubai out of ill-gotten proceeds of crime, a CBI spokesperson said. He has been taken to Raipur and produced before a special court for police remand. So far, seven Red Corner Notices and two extradition requests have been pending against other accused.The Mahadev online betting and gambling app is still active and proceeds of crime of Rs 94,000 crore have been generated so far by the accused, who are in Dubai, ED has said in its latest chargesheet in the case. More than Rs 1,000 crore has been invested in Indian share markets through foreign portfolio investments (FPIs), the agency said.It estimated that in the last few years, the accused generated more than Rs 11,000 crore annually from illegal online gambling and betting activities.Based on analysis of various seized digital evidence and statements of several accused, ED said that "it can be estimated that proceeds of crime worth Rs 11,400 crore (approx) must have been generated by illegal operations of Mahadev online book every year". The gambling network has been running since 2019."As per latest findings, Mahadev app is still running a huge number of panels. Estimated proceeds of crime generated by the app is around Rs 75,000-80,000 crore during the last seven years," ED has said. In addition, it said other illegal apps run by the syndicate like Skyexchange.com and Lotus365.com have generated proceeds of crime of over Rs 14,000 crore."A majority of the proceeds of crime was layered and transferred to the promoters based in Dubai," ED stated.The agency has so far attached assets worth over Rs 2,000 crore linked to various accused. The agency said the above estimation of proceeds of crime is only a provisional figure and is likely to go up.
Article Summary: Abhishek Kumar was deported from the UAE and taken into custody by CBI. He was close to main accused Saurabh Chandrakar and Shubham Soni. Kumar was responsible for collecting funds and acquiring immovable assets in Dubai out of ill-gotten proceeds of crime.

NEW DELHI: Meeting on the margins of United Nations General Assembly, G4 countries called for a reform of the UNSC at the earliest, saying in a joint statement that the council is currently unable to effectively discharge its core responsibility of maintaining international peace and security.The G4 group of countries (India, Japan, Brazil, and Germany) supports urgent reforms of the security council through the expansion in both permanent and non-permanent categories of membership of UNSC."Discussed the imperative of reformed multilateralism and a more representative, responsive and effective UN Security Council that reflects today's global realities. Will continue to work together to advance this shared objective," said Union external affairs minister S Jaishankar on X.The joint statement said that the representativeness, legitimacy, credibility and efficacy of UNSC are in question."They assessed that a key underlying reason is an anachronistic eight-decade-old architecture, which is not reflective of contemporary geopolitical realities and an impediment to appropriately dealing with contemporary and future challenges that humanity faces with respect to peace and security."Against this backdrop, G4 Ministers emphasised that it is crucial to implement UNSC reform at the earliest so that the council is fit-for-purpose, truly reflecting contemporary geopolitical realities."They underscored that expansion of United Nations Security Council in both permanent and non-permanent categories of membership is central to such reform and that this position is supported by a majority of member states," the statement added.
Article Summary: The G4 group of countries (India, Japan, Brazil, and Germany) supports urgent reforms of the security council through the expansion in both permanent and non- permanent categories of membership of UNSC. They assessed that a key underlying reason is an anachronistic eight-decade-old architecture.

NEW DELHI: Facing the task of implementing Supreme Court's ruling on calculating creamy layer criteria for OBC reservation from the retrospective date of 2012, Centre pleaded with the court to make the enforcement of the verdict prospective and grant it two years' time to implement it.The court had in March held that the income of parents could not be the sole criterion to determine the creamy layer of a candidate for exclusion from OBC reservation, and status and category of a parent's job had to be considered with an 'income/wealth test' as an additional criterion. It made the verdict implementable from 2012, when the case was first filed.In a written note filed by additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, govt submitted that the retrospective application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the time and create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression."The retrospective implementation of the present judgement would create changes in candidates' service and cadre allocation... as it would affect the services of persons appointed on the basis of CSE-2012 onward and cause a cascading effect among civil servants... The aforementioned cascading effect will impact not only OBC candidates but also reverberate across all categories including (unreserved category) of the civil services," the note said.Govt said a reasonable time of two years should be given to it to undertake the necessary exercise of establishing equivalence of posts, after consulting all the stakeholders and formulating a uniform policy/mechanism for determination of OBC creamy layer status."Union of India is only praying for a limited deferral of the operationalisation of the law laid down by this hon'ble court for a period of two years so that the competing rights can be adjusted consistent with the administrative contingencies and an effective equivalence exercise is carried out," it said.

Article Title: EC may order SSR of rolls in Oct for poll-bound states
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission is likely to order the special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in the poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa and Manipur in October, with January 1, 2027 as the qualifying date. However, it is unlikely to go for a nationwide special summary revision this year in view of special intensive revision (SIR) Phase 3 currently underway in 19 states/UTs and the ongoing census exercise.As per media reports, election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi are said to have objected to non-conduct of a nationwide SSR after 01.01.2025 1- an issue also amplified by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi at his press conference on Thursday. However, the sources explained that this was because SIR was underway towards the end of 2025 in a dozen states including poll-bound West Bengal, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Assam (special summary revision) and Puducherry, and had been completed only a few months back in Bihar. Besides, EC was already planning to conduct the third phase of SIR covering 19 states/UTs in 2026. The commission had to be equally mindful of the census exercise, the first phase was scheduled between April 1, 2026 and Sept 30, 2026.The second phase of census is already underway in a Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of J&K, Himachal Pradesh andUttarakhand and has been preponed in the states due for assembly polls early next year. For the rest of the country, it will follow in February 2027.The special summary revision of electoral rolls in the poll-bound states later this year will be in accordance with Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 that mandates roll revision with reference to the qualifying date before each general election to the House of the People or to the legislative assembly or a bye-election. Since the elections in the five states are to be held in February-March 2027, the updated rolls will have to be published in early January.As for the other states and UTs, sources cited sub-section 2(b) of Section 21 of R P Act, which states that revision of electoral roll every year is not mandatory and shall be revised by reference to the qualifying date "if such revision has been directed by EC".“Both SSR and SIR are done under Section 21 of RP Act 1950 and are optional. There is no legal requirement to hold both together,” an EC official told TOI.Sources said since immediate polls are not imminent in these states, there is no urgency to hold SSR. This, however, would not prevent anyone who turns 18 during this interim period, from enrolling by filling up Form 6, said an EC official.“As per the Amendment in Section 14 of RP Act 1950 in 2021 read with Section 19 of RP Act 1950, any person whose name in not on the electoral rolls or attains 18 years of age on Jan 1, 1 April 1, a July 1 or Oct 1 can register as a voter without waiting for any kind of revision as a part of regular updation of electoral rolls,” said the officer.EC is likely to wait until after the census to conduct SSR in states/UTs other than the poll-bound ones. This is essentially because the same set of field officers are involved in the roll revision and census enumeration."After SIR is completed, there has to be a reasonable period -- like a year of so -- before the next SSR is ordered as booth level officers cannot be engaged in perpetuity."

January 1, 2027 is the qualifying date. However, it is unlikely to go for a nationwide special summary revise this year in view of special intensive revision (SIR) Phase 3 currently underway in 19 states/UTs.

Article Title: Food warnings must drive reformulation, says ex-FSSAI chief
Article Text:
94% of packaged foods may face warnings under nutrient limits; FSSAI ex-chief Pawan Kumar Agarwal urges SC for phased food warning rollout

NEW DELHI: A day after FSSAI filed its compliance affidavit on front-of-pack warning labels, former FSSAI CEO Pawan Kumar Agarwal said he was comfortable with the regulator’s position, provided the transition period leads to significant improvement in the nutritional composition of packaged foods.Agarwal, through the Food Future Foundation, filed an intervention application in the Supreme Court on September 22 in the ongoing case on front-of-pack warning labels. The application seeks to assist the court on the questions it had raised on the design, scientific basis and implementation of the proposed warning system.The intervention says the transition period should drive progressive reformulation, not merely allow companies to change packaging. It proposes interim nutrient thresholds, followed by tighter limits over three to five years, with milestones and timelines announced upfront.It also recommends that any one nutrient crossing the prescribed threshold should trigger a warning, so a beverage high in sugar, for instance, cannot escape a warning because it remains below the sodium and saturated fat limits.The intervention cites a NatFirst analysis of 44,109 barcode records of packaged, branded food products available at retail in India.It found that 94.1% of the records exceeded at least one nutrient threshold, while 85.3% of those classified as high in fat, sugar and salt exceeded two or more thresholds.The figures are not weighted by sales or consumption, and NatFirst said they do not establish that individual products are unsafe, unhealthy or non-compliant. The Foundation has also proposed product-level modelling to set interim thresholds and assess their impact on warnings and reformulation.FSSAI’s September 23 affidavit proposes a single-phase rollout, with about four months to finalise the regulations, followed by a 60-day stakeholder and World Trade Organization consultation and a 365-day implementation period for food businesses. It has a red hexagon on a white square. One nutrient crossing the threshold would be named in the hexagon, while two or three would be listed together.However, NAPi has opposed putting multiple nutrients in a single hexagon, saying each nutrient should have a separate warning. It has also sought larger, bolder warnings, with their size linked to the package’s principal display area.NAPi has further called for implementation by July 2027 or earlier, instead of 2028, and questioned the use of “added sugar”, arguing that total sugar should also be considered. It cited an ICMR-NIN communication calling for the 2024 Dietary Guidelines to be applied as an integrated framework, including energy density and total nutrient levels.
Article Summary: Former FSSAI CEO Pawan Kumar Agarwal says he is comfortable with regulator's position. Food Future Foundation filed an intervention application in Supreme Court on September 22. The application seeks to assist the court on the questions it had raised on the design, scientific basis and implementation of the proposed warning system.

Article Title: SC flags ‘false’ POCSO cases in marital disputes, bars immediate arrest of accused parent
Article Text:
Rape-murder of A law student: Petitioner Ameer-Ul-Islam seeking transfer from Viyyur Central Prison in Kerala to a jail in Assam

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday laid down safeguards against the immediate arrest of a parent or family member accused under the POCSO Act when the alleged offence involves a child living under the same roof and there is a matrimonial dispute between the child's parents.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan, flagging a rise in fakecases, said police should not act in haste in such cases and directed that, as a general rule, an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology should evaluate the child before authorities decide whether there is sufficient reason to arrest the accused.The court said the safeguards were necessary in cases where allegations may be influenced by a strained relationship between the parents. It stressed that the measures do not dilute the seriousness of offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, but are intended to ensure that the power of arrest is exercised after considering all relevant circumstances.The court said immediate arrest should not take place when two conditions are present: a POCSO offence is alleged against a parent or family member living with the child, and a matrimonial dispute exists between the child's parents, whether or not the dispute is pending before a court.The police officer receiving the complaint must verify whether such a matrimonial dispute exists, the court said. "When the above-stated threshold conditions are met, post the registration of an FIR, we are of the considered opinion that the investigating officer should not act in haste or take coercive actions in the form of arrest immediately," the bench added, as quoted by PTI.The verdict came in a matrimonial dispute involving an estranged Bengaluru couple. The wife had alleged that the child was sexually assaulted. The case was investigated by the CBI, which found the allegation to be false. The Supreme Court restored custody of the child to the father, taking into account the welfare of the minor.The court also directed the investigating officer or the Special Juvenile Police Unit to seek the services of an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology, in consultation with the District Child Protection Unit or, where one is unavailable, the District Legal Services Authority, adding that the expert's evaluation must be conducted independently and without influence from either the parent or investigating authorities.After receiving the evaluation, investigators must consider the expert's opinion along with other evidence and circumstances before deciding whether there is "reason to believe" that the accused committed the offence and whether an arrest is warranted. The court said an exception could be made in cases where the material available is "palpable", allowing the investigating officer to dispense with an expert evaluation, but reasons for doing so must be recorded in writing.The bench also stressed that arrest is not automatically required merely because an offence is cognisable. The court said an arrest can cause "irreparable harm" to an accused parent or family member, particularly where the allegation later turns out to be unfounded.The Supreme Court also raised concerns about the consequences of allegations on children and their relationship with the accused parent."The trauma that a child is put through in the process and the accusation can damage the very fabric of the parent-child relationship," the bench said, adding that such a wound could leave an "indelible scar" on both the child and parent.The court also flagged what it described as an increase in false allegations in matrimonial disputes."What is alarming is that this tendency of making false accusations is on the rise," it said.The bench cautioned against parents being influenced by advisers during matrimonial disputes, saying that some may be driven by a "win at any cost" approach.At the same time, the court said the safeguards were not a finding that allegations made in such circumstances are false. Investigating authorities must examine the allegations along with the surrounding circumstances and other evidence.For complaints filed directly before a special court, the Supreme Court said an order taking cognisance and summoning an accused must demonstrate application of mind. The special court should also involve an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology to evaluate the child and submit a report.
Article Summary: Supreme Court lays down safeguards against the immediate arrest of a parent or family member accused under the POCSO Act. Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said police should not act in haste in such cases. The safeguards were necessary in cases where allegations may be influenced by a strained relationship between the parents.

Now, there is no trust in the Election Commission," Yadav said.The PDA acronym, coined by Yadav in 2023, refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities).Yadav alleged that the BJP was using the election machinery because it knew people would not vote for the party on issues such as inflation.He claimed that the alleged "vote theft" in the 2022 Assembly polls had prevented the SP from forming the government in Uttar Pradesh.The SP chief also attacked what he described as "bulldozer politics", saying the PDA movement would challenge it in the 2027 elections."This time (in 2027) the electoral verdict would not merely defeat them but would 'demolish' and permanently eliminate such negative politics," he said.Yadav also referred to the 2024 Lok Sabha election, saying, "We defeated them in 2024 and in 2027 we will work for their (BJP) permanent defeat."The SP and Congress had contested the 2024 Lok Sabha election in Uttar Pradesh as allies, winning 37 and six seats respectively, for a combined tally of 43. The BJP won 33 seats in the state.Yadav said the SP would contest the 2027 polls as part of an alliance, although he did not specify its partners or the number of seats each party would contest."We will have an alliance," he said, adding that the basis for deciding seats would be winnability."Whoever can win a seat should get that seat," Yadav asserted.His remarks come as the SP and Congress face the question of whether they can maintain their alliance for the next Uttar Pradesh Assembly election.Yadav's PDA Rath campaign was launched from Raebareli, where Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is the sitting Lok Sabha MP. The SP had said Yadav's visit also included a planned meeting with Harchandpur MLA Rahul Lodhi, following a September 17 clash involving members of the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha and ABVP.Police had denied allegations of manhandling by SP workers and said a magisterial inquiry into the police action had been ordered.The specially designed PDA Rath carries slogans including "Samajwadi PDA Yatra" and "PDA hi parivartan layega", along with the definition of PDA as Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak.Yadav also criticised the BJP over the alleged demolition of religious structures in Kashi and Saharanpur, accusing the party of pursuing communal politics and weakening social harmony.On the proposed Uniform Civil Code , he said laws should follow efforts to ensure equality among citizens."We say first make the citizens equal; first, let all of us become one. When everyone's respect becomes equal, then bring laws to increase that respect and take people forward," he said.On employment, Yadav promised that an SP government would increase government recruitment and provide jobs to young people."If outsourcing has to be ended, we will end outsourcing," he said.He also promised free treatment in hospitals, saying people would not have to search for a card before receiving healthcare.Yadav accused the state government of shutting primary schools while opening liquor shops and said an SP government would reopen schools that had been closed.He also promised to restore the old pension scheme for government employees.The Raebareli visit marks the beginning of the SP's PDA-focused outreach ahead of the 2027 Assembly election, with Yadav using the campaign to reiterate his allegations against the Election Commission, outline his alliance strategy and present the party's key electoral promises.

Article Title: Government expands the list of permitted chemicals for storage in coastal areas
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a move that may boost port-adjacent industries by allowing storage of specific chemicals in coastal areas, the govt has expanded the list of petroleum and chemical products permitted for storage in the coastal regulation zone (CRZ) by amending the existing CRZ notification, 2019.The amendment, published by the Union environment ministry on Thursday, now provides for storing 26 petroleum and chemical products in the coastal areas instead of 23 such products permitted earlier. The additional products are linear alkyl benzene, N-paraffin and carbon black feedstock.The list of 23 already permitted products includes crude oil, LPG, kerosene, aviation fuel, high-speed diesel, lubricating oil, CNG, naphtha, acetic acid, methanol, liquefied natural gas and furnace oil, among others.The amendment was notified to accommodate formal representations made by various State Coastal Zone Management Authorities to facilitate the industrial receipt and storage of these specific chemicals in coastal areas. The decision was finally taken after the sectoral Expert Appraisal Committee for CRZ clearances and the National Coastal Zone Management Authority gave their nod.The ministry’s notification said that National Coastal Zone Management Authority, after due deliberation, considering the comparatively lower hazardous chemical characteristics of these products in relation to those already permitted, “unanimously recommended allowing the receipt and storage of Linear Alkyl Benzene, N-Paraffin, and Carbon Black Feedstock in CRZ areas”, excluding Coastal Regulation Zone-IA, through the necessary amendment.It means these products will not be allowed for storage in the environmentally most critical CRZ-IA areas (like mangroves, coral reefs, and turtle nesting grounds) along the coastline. This zone plays a vital role in maintaining the structural integrity of the coast and acting as a natural defence against hazards like cyclones, storms, and tsunamis.
Article Summary: The amendment, published by the Union environment ministry on Thursday, now provides for storing 26 petroleum and chemical products in the coastal areas. The additional products are linear alkyl benzene, N-paraffin and carbon black feedstock. The decision was finally taken after the sectoral Expert Appraisal Committee for CRZ clearances and the National Coastal Zone Management Authority gave their nod.

NEW DELHI: Union power ministry has finalised the draft National Electricity Policy (NEP) and moved the Cabinet note for inter-ministerial consultation.Released in Jan this year, the draft National Electricity Policy has proposed index-linked automatic annual tariff revision, sought to limit cross-subsidies for the manufacturing sector and railways, increase nuclear capacity, repurpose older thermal units for grid support, and take measures to reduce transmission and distribution losses.Union power secretary Pankaj Agarwal said the ministry received a number of comments and suggestions from stakeholders, which were subsequently examined and accommodated in the draft policy.“We have aggregated all the stakeholders’ comments. We have already moved the Cabinet note for inter-ministerial consultation and I think it shouldn’t be taking very long,” Agarwal told reporters on the sidelines of the 2nd Indian Power Sector Conference organised by Ficci.The last NEP was notified in 2005, when the sector was facing challenges such as demand-supply gaps, limited electricity access and inadequate infrastructure.“Today we are at a very different level...we are already at 300 gigawatt of non-fossil and now going forward, the challenges are entirely different like grid management and building transmission systems,” he said.With the rise in renewable energy, grid stability has emerged as a major challenge, along with under-utilisation of transmission lines during non-solar hours.Agarwal said grid utilisation was also a dimension of NEP 2026. “You can't expect it to be utilised 24x7 at a particular level. There will be more fluctuations. If we can really use 60% of grid capacity, I think that’s a fairly good thing,” he said.The power secretary also said steps were being taken to indigenously design and produce chips for smart meters and the ministry had mandated requirements for their manufacturing, along with timelines. He added that some of the designs had to be tested and validated before commercial production began.
Article Summary: The draft National Electricity Policy has proposed index-linked automatic annual tariff revision. It also sought to limit cross-subsidies for the manufacturing sector and railways. The last NEP was notified in 2005, when the sector was facing challenges such as demand-supply gaps.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Thursday escalated his attack on the Centre and the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that India's elections had been "rigged" and demanding the immediate resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Congress MP said Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and Kumar were "deshdrohis" (traitors) for what he alleged was the destruction of the country's vote.He said the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were "all rigged" and asserted that PM Modi and Shah would be investigated over what he described as a conspiracy to "steal elections".His remarks came a day after an investigation by a media report claimed that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally raised objections to decisions and orders related to electoral-roll management and the SIR exercise.The Election Commission has rejected the suggestion that these objections reflected a disagreement over its final decisions, saying its decisions, including those concerning SIR, were unanimous.Addressing a press conference at the Congress headquarters in New Delhi, Rahul said the Election Commission was responsible for protecting the vote and accused the poll panel of failing in that duty."Mr Gyanesh Kumar must resign immediately. We are not going to let democracy be destroyed in India and sit silent, and the people responsible for this are going to be punished," Rae Bareli MP said.He said the reported objections by Sandhu and Joshi showed that questions were being raised within the poll panel itself."The two Election Commissioners have done a wise thing, and I appreciate it," he said.Former Congress president further alleged that the Prime Minister and home minister were "at the top of this conspiracy" and would be investigated. He also suggested that Kumar should "turn approver", describing that as an act of nationalism."I can say with certainty that Indian elections -- 2024 Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha polls -- were all rigged," Rahul said.He also linked the alleged manipulation of votes to the functioning of Parliament, laws and institutions."From vote chori (vote theft), comes kanoon chori (law theft) and from that comes sanstha chori (institutional theft)," he said.Explaining the argument, the Congress leader said the vote was the foundation of the constitutional system."If the vote has been destroyed, then our Constitution has been destroyed. If our Constitution has been destroyed, our laws are illegal. If our laws are illegal, our institutions are meaningless," he said.He said the alleged issue was therefore not limited to electoral rolls but concerned the wider constitutional framework."The central question here is this is not just an attack on the vote; this is an attack on the idea, the basic infrastructure, and the expression of every single Indian person," Rahul said.The immediate trigger was an Indian Express investigation reporting that Sandhu and Joshi recorded at least 14 objections over 10 months to decisions and orders issued in the name of the Election Commission.The objections reportedly covered voter registration and deletion, changes to Form 6 used for new voter registration, access to and centralisation of electoral-roll databases, and other aspects of the SIR exercise.The report said the two commissioners had objected four times on a single day and had raised concerns about decisions they said were taken without their knowledge or approval.The Election Commission, however, has disputed the interpretation that the reported internal notes amounted to a breakdown or disagreement over final decisions.The poll panel said internal technical notes, queries and suggestions were part of the normal administrative and decision-making process and maintained that the final decisions of the Commission were unanimous. Its response did not dispute the existence of the notes but said focusing on individual objections presented only part of the overall decision-making process.The EC's position is that all decisions relating to SIR had the approval of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners Sandhu and Joshi.The BJP hit back at Lok Sabha LoP's allegations, with party spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari describing his press conference as a "damp squib" and dubbing it "Jhoot Ki Goonj".In a post on X, Bhandari accused Rahul of making false claims and said the Congress leader was unable to win public support through democratic means.He also challenged Rahul's assertion that there had been no anti-incumbency against the BJP since 2014, saying the BJP had lost 20 elections since then.BJP leader and MP Sudhanshu Trivedi also challenged Rae Bareli MP's argument on anti-incumbency.He pointed to the Congress's electoral record in states including Tamil Nadu and West Bengal and argued that anti-incumbency had affected the Congress as well.On the media report, Trivedi questioned the basis for treating the reported objections as evidence that the Election Commission's final decisions were not unanimous."Do you have even a single report indicating that a decision was not unanimous?" Trivedi said, adding that there was no quoted statement from any Election Commissioner saying that a final decision had not been unanimous.He also questioned whether the reported internal objections should be treated as evidence of a wider institutional dispute when the Commission had maintained that its decisions were unanimous.A significant part of the Congress leader's press conference focused on what he described as the disappearance of anti-incumbency against the BJP.He cited electoral swings in Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, and said governments and political parties in India had historically faced anti-incumbency."Haryana swings from one party to another for 50 years. Suddenly anti-incumbency disappears. Maharashtra swings; suddenly it disappears. Uttar Pradesh swings. Sometimes Samajwadi, sometimes BSP; it disappears. Madhya Pradesh, it disappears. Gujarat, it disappears," Rahul said.He cited former prime minister Indira Gandhi's experience after the 1971 Bangladesh war as an example of how anti-incumbency, according to him, had affected even highly popular leaders."It happens to leader after leader. It does not happen to PM Modi, Shah and the BJP - now we know the answer to it," he said.He also played videos of PM Modi and Shah, including remarks about the BJP remaining in power for decades and Modi's "Abki Baar 400 Paar" slogan. He argued that such statements were inconsistent with the normal operation of democratic politics.However, BJP has rejected Rahul's allegations, while the Election Commission has maintained that the reported objections were part of its internal decision-making process and that its final decisions, including those related to SIR, were unanimous.The dispute over the electoral-roll revision and the reported objections by the two election commissioners is now at the centre of the political exchange between Congress, BJP and the poll panel.
Article Summary: Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi escalated his attack on the Centre and the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He demanded the immediate resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul said Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and Kumar were "deshdrohis"

Article Title: 'We know what delay did in Shiv Sena': On TMC symbol row, SC asks EC to set time limit for final decision
Article Text:
The Election Commission has barred both Trinamool Congress factions from using the party's name.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Election Commission to give rival factions in the Trinamool Congress dispute reasonable time to present their evidence, but to ensure that the proceedings are completed in time for the upcoming West Bengal elections.The court's direction came against the backdrop of the prolonged Shiv Sena name-and-symbol dispute. "We know what delay did in Shiv Sena," the bench observed, stressing that the TMC dispute should not be allowed to drag on indefinitely, according to news agency ANI.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a plea filed by former West Bengal chief minister and TMC leader Mamata Banerjee challenging the Election Commission's decision concerning the use of the original TMC name and its traditional 'Flowers and Grass' symbol.The court asked the Election Commission how much time it would need to complete the adjudication, particularly since its order was intended to operate for the current by-election.The bench said that while the dispute needed to be resolved within a reasonable timeframe, both sides must have adequate opportunity to place their evidence before the poll panel.Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Mamata Banerjee, sought a stay on the Election Commission's order, submitting that it had left his client without an effective remedy."EC order has left me without a remedy," Sibal said.The Supreme Court said it was conscious of the consequences of delay in disputes involving the identity of political parties and their election symbols.The court asked the Election Commission to provide the rival sides reasonable time to submit their evidence and complete the adjudication sufficiently ahead of the West Bengal elections.
Article Summary: The Election Commission has barred both Trinamool Congress factions from using the party's name. The Supreme Court asked the Election Commission to provide the rival sides reasonable time to submit their evidence and complete the adjudication sufficiently ahead of the West Bengal elections. "We know what delay did in Shiv Sena," the bench observed.

Article Title: POCSO case cannot be quashed on settlement, says Delhi HC
Article Text:
“POCSO offence cannot be quashed on basis of compromise”, says Delhi High Court

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has held that proceedings under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act cannot be quashed on the basis of a compromise between a child victim or the victim's family and the accused.Justice Sachin Datta made the observation while dismissing a petition seeking quashing of an FIR and related proceedings on the basis of a settlement allegedly reached with the victim with the intervention of her family, according to news agency ANI.The court noted that the case involved allegations of aggravated penetrative sexual assault against a child by a person allegedly in a position of trust or authority. It observed that such offences are heinous and have a serious impact on society.The high court relied on a Supreme Court judgment which held that while a high court has inherent powers to quash criminal proceedings in appropriate cases where parties have settled their dispute, such powers must be exercised after considering the nature and gravity of the offence.The Supreme Court has held that heinous and serious offences, including rape, ordinarily cannot be quashed merely because the victim or the victim’s family and the accused have reached a settlement, as such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society.Applying the principle, the Delhi high court held that an offence under the POCSO Act cannot be compromised by the child victim or the victim’s family. It said quashing the proceedings at this stage on the basis of a compromise would defeat the object of the statute and the ends of justice.

Case involved allegations of aggravated penetrative sexual assault against a child by a person allegedly in a position of trust or authority. High court relied on a Supreme Court judgment which held that while a high court has inherent powers to quash criminal proceedings in appropriate cases.
